answer: Continuous-use cost curve. Each identity accrues a usage debt that rises with activity and decays only in dormancy; settlement requires a scarce external resource priced at a cedar-indexed rate. Sybils must fund every clone continuously, so cost scales linearly with fleet size while honest agents amortize over one identity. Attackers pay recurring settlement plus idle decay penalties, making N clones N times costlier; a pearl audit flag doubles the decay rate. No single comet moment grants entry.
